question: According to the Statistical Appendix of the Economic Survey 2023-24, what was India's Infant Mortality Rate (IMR) in 2020?
solution:
The correct answer is __**28 per 1000 live births**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• India's Infant Mortality Rate (IMR) in 2020 was recorded as **28 per 1000 live births** according to the Statistical Appendix of the Economic Survey 2023-24.
 
• This represents a **significant improvement** in reducing infant mortality rates over the years.
 
• The reduction in IMR is attributed to various government health initiatives and increased healthcare access.
 
• Programs such as the **National Rural Health Mission (NRHM)** and **Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY)** have played a crucial role in this improvement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Infant Mortality Rate (IMR)**

 
 
• IMR is defined as the number of deaths of infants under one year old per 1,000 live births in a given year.
 
• It is a crucial indicator of the overall health condition of a population.
 
• High IMR indicates poor health infrastructure, while a low IMR reflects better health services and maternal care.
 
 
 
• **National Rural Health Mission (NRHM)**
 
 
• Launched in 2005, NRHM aims to provide accessible, affordable, and quality healthcare to the rural population, especially the vulnerable groups.
 
• It focuses on strengthening healthcare infrastructure and improving maternal and child health.
 
 
 
• **Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY)**
 
 
• JSY is a safe motherhood intervention under the National Health Mission (NHM).
 
• It aims to reduce maternal and neonatal mortality by promoting institutional delivery among poor pregnant women.
 
 
 
• **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**
 
 
• IMR reduction is a part of the broader framework of the SDGs, specifically Goal 3, which aims to ensure healthy lives and promote well-being for all at all ages.
 
• Targets under Goal 3 include ending preventable deaths of newborns and children under 5 years of age by 2030.
